2_Introduction: PSC with device efficiency (PCE) of 23.0865%, VOC of 1.1364 V, JSC of 24.931 mA/cm², and FF of 81.4858% was obtained. 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with the composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then 5000 rpm for 40 s. At 10 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure, 160 µL CB was dropped onto the substrates. The film was then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), enhancing phase stability while suppressing halide segregation and Pb⁰/I⁻ vacancy formation; the low-dimensional Cs⁺ incorporation rigidifies the lattice and mitigates thermal-driven ion migration, whereas FA⁺ dominates the B–X octahedral framework to maintain a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.53 eV and high dielectric screening, and the precise stoichiometry (X = 3.0) eliminates excess PbI₂-induced trap states. Crystallization is kinetically controlled by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) ensures uniform wet-film formation and precursor wetting, while the high-speed phase (5000 rpm, 40 s) governs solvent evaporation rate and supersaturation buildup, with antisolvent dripping (160 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s pre-end) triggering instantaneous nucleation by rapidly extracting DMF/DMSO, thereby promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing Ostwald ripening—this yields large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area, as corroborated by high-film-coverage optical imaging showing >98% continuity and minimal pinhole density, while time-resolved PL mapping reveals uniformly elevated intensity and monoexponential decay with τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.24 µs, indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination across the entire active area. XRD analysis confirms phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ with no detectable δ-phase or residual PbI₂ (absence of the 12.6° peak), sharp (110) reflection with narrow FWHM (0.12°), and absence of strain-splitting peaks—collectively evidencing complete crystalline conversion, minimal microstrain, and high structural homogeneity. The resulting interfacial defect landscape is intrinsically minimized not only by stoichiometric precision and kinetic control but also by the self-organized passivation arising from the cation distribution itself: FA⁺’s steric bulk suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ at grain surfaces, Cs⁺ segregates to grain boundaries to terminate dangling bonds, and MA⁺’s intermediate size modulates lattice relaxation at heterointerfaces, collectively passivating both shallow and deep traps without requiring exogenous ligands. This intrinsic, compositionally encoded passivation synergizes with the antisolvent-mediated crystallization dynamics to yield a film with low Urbach energy (22 meV), high carrier diffusion length (>2.1 µm), and balanced electron/hole extraction—ultimately delivering VOC of 1.1364 V, JSC of 24.931 mA/cm², FF of 81.4858%, and PCE of 23.0865%.
